title: Pilot: Privacy & SLA review — sizing, benchmarks, prompt archiving
summary: Initial pilot scoping for a 4-week privacy-first inference pilot. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing (concurrent sessions, tokens/sec), benchmark plan, data handling constraints (PII redaction, prompt storage, retention), and next steps for security artifacts and pilot schedule.
topics: Prompt storage and retention policy options
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark script and tokenized sample workload (by 2025-10-02)
CedarFin to share example prompts & PII types (by 2025-10-01)
Redwood to provide security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption docs) and KMS flow (by 2025-10-03)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send benchmark harness + run instructions; due 2025-10-02
Priya Rao: Share 3 days of production-ish prompts and sample records; due 2025-10-01
Liam O'Connor: Draft data flow diagram showing redaction + retention points; due 2025-10-03
Ethan Miles: Confirm KMS policy and whether HSM is required; due 2025-10-05
transcript:
HEADER: 2025-09-29 15:00 UTC — Duration 62m — Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (CedarFin Head of Data), Ethan (CedarFin Security), Nora (CedarFin ML)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call. I'm Maya Chen, AE on the account. Liam's here for the bench and tech details.
00:14 - Priya: Hi all, Priya here. We're looking to scope a short pilot to validate privacy controls and perf.
00:21 - Liam: Quick note — I'll be focused on the benchmarking harness and redaction approach.
00:35 - Ethan: Thanks. Security's top concern: we need assurance around PII exfil, retention settings, and KMS flow.
01:03 - Maya: Great. Agenda: agree success criteria, sizing, bench plan, and data handling guardrails.
02:10 - Priya: For success, primary is latency at 200ms median for single-turn customer queries, second is no sensitive data logged, and third is throughput for batch scoring — around 150 qps at 1k tokens average.
02:45 - Liam: We'll need more detail on token distribution. If most calls are 600-1k tokens, that changes batching. Also caching/prefix reuse can help.
03:30 - Nora: Most prompts are transactional: account lookups, KYC-like free text, and some attachments meta. There will be occasional long prompts for document summarize — ~2k tokens.
04:05 - Ethan: The attachments metadata can contain names/IDs — these are definitely PII. We must not store raw prompts beyond 24h in pilot, ideally no prompt storage at all.
05:00 - Maya: Understood. We offer several options: 1) do not persist prompts (ephemeral only), 2) persist prompts but redact PII client-side before sending, 3) persist prompts encrypted at rest with KMS and limited retention.
05:36 - Priya: Option 2 is attractive but would require good redaction coverage. Option 3 is more realistic because we want to inspect logs for failure repro. But retention must be configurable to 24h.
06:20 - Liam: Technical caveat — full post-hoc redaction is tricky if models output echoed sensitive tokens. We can do dynamic redaction pre-ingest using regex + entity recognition. We also have a pseudo-anonymization service (hashing plus salt) if you need referential ids preserved but not raw values.
07:05 - Priya: Can we do client-side redaction? We have a pipeline that can annotate PII entities and replace them with placeholders.
07:40 - Liam: Yes, you can do client-side. For the pilot we can show both: client redaction + server-side additional checks. Server-side will mark any prompt that appears to contain high-risk PII and reject ingest unless flagged for manual review.
08:12 - Ethan: About prompt storage: we require audit logs showing who accessed what and when. Also SAML SSO for access to console and RBAC controls per team. Do you support session-level audit trails?
08:45 - Maya: Console has token-level traces and per-route logs. We can surface access logs and tie to your SSO identity. We will provide the SOC2 summary and an export format for audit logs.
09:20 - Priya: Great. How about KMS? We use an internal HSM-backed KMS. We prefer customer-managed keys.
09:46 - Liam: We support bring-your-own-KMS (via API) for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted pilot, we can do envelope encryption with your key, or if needed we can spin a dedicated pool with your KMS integrated. There's a slight perf hit for every token encryption op, but we can minimize by encrypting only persisted artifacts (e.g., logs, stored prompts).
10:25 - Nora: For benchmarks — what do you want from us?
10:40 - Liam: We'll send a harness (script + sample payloads) that reproduces your qps distribution and token lengths. We request a small dataset (1000 synthetic requests matching production distribution) plus real-ish sample prompts. We'll run baseline on our fastest hosted model and then on ded. pool if you request.
11:10 - Priya: Timeline? We want results within two weeks of getting the sample. Pilot kickoff in about 1 week if security pack exchanged.
11:30 - Maya: Proposed: week 1 — security review + exchange creds, week 2 — run bench and tune, week 3 — short functional tests with redaction, week 4 — evaluation and next-step decision. That fits a 4-week pilot.
12:05 - Ethan: Success gates: median latency under 300ms for single-turn; p95 under 800ms; throughput hitting 80% of target qps; no unredacted PII in persisted logs after redaction rules run; documented KMS flow.
12:40 - Maya: We'll capture those as the pilot SLOs. Also include cost projection: token cost per 1M tokens and infra cost for dedicated pool.
13:05 - Priya: Regarding cost, if we need dedicated due to KMS or tenancy, what's the commit? We're trying to avoid a big upfront if possible.
13:25 - Maya: For pilot, we can offer a limited reserved pool with short-term commit and an overage rate. We'll include pricing options in the doc.
13:55 - Nora: A question on prompt archiving: we sometimes need to retain prompts for debugging but we can store sanitized versions. Does Redwood support storing both raw and redacted traces separately with different retention?
14:20 - Liam: Yes. We can store redacted traces as the canonical audit log (longer retention), and raw traces encrypted under customer KMS with 24h auto-delete. The UI and export APIs will only surface redacted versions unless you explicitly request a raw export (audit) with extra access controls.
15:10 - Priya: What's your redaction accuracy? Are you using an ML NER model plus regex?
15:26 - Liam: We use a hybrid approach: rule-based regex for sensitive patterns (SSNs, emails) and an entity model tuned for names, addresses. For the pilot we'll share false positive/negative estimates — but we recommend client-side token replacement for ultra-sensitive fields.
16:05 - Ethan: We'll need that FP/FN estimate for compliance review. Also need to know how you log model outputs — do you keep generated tokens?
16:25 - Maya: Model outputs may be logged for observability, but we can route outputs to a separate retention tier and apply redaction there too. By default outputs are ephemeral and only stored if trace is enabled.
17:00 - Priya: On benchmarking metrics, please capture: median/p95 latency, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
17:25 - Liam: Agreed. We'll report those and upload raw bench results and profiler traces. We'll also surface KV cache hit rates if you use repeated prefixes.
18:10 - Nora: We do have reuse — about 12% of requests reuse the same session prefix. Can caching help for p95?
18:35 - Liam: Yes, prefix KV caching reduces compute and latency for repeated contexts. We'll instrument it in the harness.
19:00 - Priya: Any limitations around attachments or binary data?
19:20 - Maya: Attachments must be preprocessed client-side; we can accept metadata and a link to storage. We do not ingest raw binaries into the model input in hosted pilot — you can implement a preprocess step to transform into text.
20:05 - Ethan: For legal, procurement will want the retention config in the SOW. Will you include configurable retention periods per artifact type?
20:25 - Maya: Yes — console supports retention knobs per artifact (prompts, outputs, logs). For the pilot we'll set prompts raw to 24h, redacted logs to 90 days, outputs ephemeral unless trace enabled. All configurable.
21:10 - Priya: Is there a way to do automatic deletion API if we trigger an incident?
21:25 - Liam: We have purge APIs to delete artifacts by date range or id. For HSM-backed keys, deleting the key renders data unrecoverable as an additional option.
22:00 - Maya: Let's recap next steps — we'll send the benchmark harness, security pack, and a proposed SOW with retention defaults. CedarFin will provide sample prompts and confirm KMS/HSM requirements.
22:25 - Priya: Agreed. Also we'll prepare a short list of test accounts and a staging dataset.
22:40 - Nora: Minor note — for evaluating accuracy we want to include 200 labeled examples for the summarization use case.
23:00 - Liam: Noted — include those in the sample. We'll run a quality regression test against the labeled set.
23:30 - Ethan: One last callout: we will want a short window of canary traffic to dedicated if we move to dedicated after pilot. Can you support a hybrid route?
23:50 - Maya: Yes, smart routing supports canary by percentage and region. We'll draft a canary plan in the SOW.
24:10 - Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll look for the artifacts and target kickoff next week.
24:30 - Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with dates and the attachments.
24:45 - Meeting ends.
